properties.description: The Immaculate Conception of Little Dizzle (2010), written and directed by David Russo and starring Marshall Allman, Jeanette Maus, and Sean Nelson, is an indie comedy-drama that follows a dislocated young man who takes a night janitor job at a market-research firm. He and his ragtag crew uncover clandestine experiments that lead to bizarre side effects, propelling the film into surreal and blackly comedic territory. Combining satirical commentary on corporate life with religious undertones and striking visual effects, the movie examines faith, identity, and exploitation through an offbeat, character-driven lens.
properties.plot_summary: After losing his steady job, a disoriented young man takes a night janitor position at a market-research firm and joins a ragged crew of nocturnal cleaners. While working late he uncovers clandestine experiments on employees that produce bizarre, escalating side effects. As the group's lives unravel, surreal imagery and black comedy mix with questions of faith, identity, and exploitation. The film follows his strange initiation into a world where corporate routine mutates into disturbing, unpredictable madness.

properties.description: Project Power (2020), directed by Ariel Schulman and Henry Joost and starring Jamie Foxx, Joseph Gordon-Levitt and Dominique Fishback, is a sci-fi action thriller about a mysterious pill that grants users unpredictable superpowers for five minutes. Set against New Orleans' urban landscape, the film follows a teenage dealer, a cop and an ex-soldier as their hunt for the pill's source exposes a broader conspiracy and systemic corruption. The movie mixes high-octane action and inventive visual effects with themes of addiction, power and social inequality, balancing explosive set pieces with moral and emotional stakes. The tone is gritty and adrenaline-driven, anchored by dynamic performances and a propulsive soundtrack.
properties.plot_summary: When a pill that grants unpredictable superpowers for five minutes spreads through the streets of New Orleans, a teenage dealer, a local cop and an ex-soldier form an uneasy alliance to find its source. Their investigation into distribution networks and corrupt interests uncovers a larger conspiracy tied to illicit experiments. As turf wars and betrayals escalate, the trio must confront moral compromises and rising violence while racing to shut down the operation before more people are harmed.

properties.description: True Story (2015), directed by Rupert Goold and starring James Franco, Jonah Hill, and Felicity Jones, is a crime drama based on Michael Finkel's nonfiction account of a real criminal case. The film follows a disgraced reporter who seeks out an accused murderer using his name; their encounters become a manipulative, psychological cat-and-mouse that tests truth, identity, and journalistic ethics. Performed in a moody, intimate style, the movie explores themes of deception, obsession, and the ethical cost of storytelling while maintaining tense, investigative pacing. The tone is unsettling and morally ambiguous, anchored by performances that emphasize the characters' conflicted inner lives.
properties.plot_summary: A disgraced reporter contacts an accused murderer who has been using his name, hoping the connection will revive his career. Their meetings evolve into a manipulative cat-and-mouse game in which truth, identity, and motive are continually disputed. As the journalist digs deeper, the relationship becomes a psychological battle that blurs professional boundaries and moral clarity. The story examines how storytelling, media attention, and personal ambition complicate the search for facts in a high-profile criminal case.

properties.description: Bodyguards and Assassins (2009), directed by Teddy Chan and starring Xueqi Wang, Tony Ka Fai Leung and Jun Hu, is a Hong Kong historical action-drama about an assassination plot against a visiting revolutionary leader. The ensemble piece develops the backgrounds and motivations of a diverse group of protectors before mounting extended, high-energy combat sequences as the threat unfolds. Themes of sacrifice, loyalty, and collective struggle for political change are central, and the film mixes emotional character drama with large-scale period action.
properties.plot_summary: In the early 1900s, revolutionaries in British-controlled Hong Kong learn that assassins have been sent to kill a visiting political leader, so they recruit a disparate group of protectors to escort him to a secret meeting. The film spends time developing the backstories and motivations of its ensemble cast, showing why each person is willing to risk everything for the cause. As the plot advances, the narrative shifts into tightly choreographed action and escalating confrontations, and several characters make painful sacrifices to ensure the leader's safety and the movement's survival.

properties.description: Julia X (directed by P.J. Pettiette) is a dark comedy-horror thriller starring Valerie Azlynn, Kevin Sorbo, and Alicia Leigh Willis. properties.description: Marvelous and the Black Hole (2021), directed by Kate Tsang and starring Miya Cech, Rhea Perlman, and Leonardo Nam, is a comedy-drama about a grieving teenage girl who forms an unlikely bond with a surly children’s party magician. The film follows Sammy as she struggles with her mother’s death, family tensions, and rebellious behavior, then gradually channels her turmoil into learning magic and reconnecting with her family. Through quiet humor and emotional honesty, the story examines grief, mentorship, and coming-of-age transformation with a warm, intimate tone.

Sammy begins to channel her anger into learning magic, which opens pathways to reconnect with her father and sister and to face her grief. Over the course of their relationship, the two women help each other confront loneliness, responsibility, and the possibility of healing.

properties.description: Lost in the Pacific (2016), directed by Vincent Zhou and starring Brandon Routh, Yuqi Zhang, and Russell Wong, is a sci‑fi adventure-thriller about the ill-fated maiden flight of a prototype transoceanic airliner. The film leans heavily on polished visual effects and action sequences while exploring themes of trust, sacrifice, and teamwork. Its emotional register mixes suspense and adrenaline with occasional moments of levity.

The film emphasizes high‑octane action and spectacle as the ensemble struggles to cooperate, sacrifice when necessary, and survive long enough to be rescued.

properties.description: Spaghetti (2023), directed by Adam Gierasch and starring Angie Stevenson, Sarah Nicklin, and Kara Talley, is a drama-thriller with strong supernatural and horror overtones. The film follows a nurse who, suspecting her partner of infidelity, takes her friend's advice and uses a voodoo ritual to intervene; the consequences escalate from uneasy suspicion to psychological unraveling. Through its slow-burn pacing, atmospheric cinematography, and uncanny score, the film interrogates themes of jealousy, obsession, revenge, and the moral fallout of trying to control love. The emotional tone is brooding and unsettling, occasionally leavened by darkly comic touches but ultimately building toward a nightmarish climax.

properties.description: See You Tomorrow (2016), directed by Jiajia Zhang and starring Tony Leung Chiu-wai, Takeshi Kaneshiro and Eason Chan, is a comedy-drama-romance that follows a bar owner who serves as an emotional 'ferryman' for a circle of lonely people while confronting his own past. Told through a sequence of intimate vignettes, the film emphasizes lyrical visuals, monologues and music as it explores memory, regret and the quiet work of healing. Stylistically it leans toward arthouse moodiness and nostalgic imagery, and tonally it blends tenderness with melancholy to create a reflective, character-driven experience.
properties.plot_summary: A bar owner known as a self-styled 'ferryman' quietly shepherds a circle of damaged people through their small, private crises while he slowly confronts his own traumatic past. Through late-night conversations, music and small acts of care he helps a co-partner, a singer and a neighbor face loneliness and regret. The film unfolds as a series of intimate character vignettes that reveal how memory, longing and small mercies shape personal recovery. Tonally it moves between tenderness and melancholy, letting monologues and visual mood carry much of the emotional weight.

properties.description: Carry On Jatta (2012), directed by Smeep Kang and starring Gippy Grewal, Mahie Gill and Gurpreet Ghuggi, is a Punjabi-language comedy built around a romantic farce. properties.description: The Girl Who Killed Her Parents: The Confession (2023), directed by Maurício Eça and starring Carla Diaz, Leonardo Bittencourt, and Allan Souza Lima, is a Portuguese-language crime drama that revisits the investigation behind the murders of the Richthofen couple. Presented as a spin-off follow-up to an earlier film, this installment concentrates on the police work, evidence, and interviews that culminated in the prosecution of Suzane von Richthofen and the Cravinhos brothers. The production leans into a gritty, documentary-influenced aesthetic while exploring themes of guilt, family betrayal, and the pursuit of justice. Emotionally, the film is tense and unsettling, aimed at viewers drawn to methodical reconstructions of real criminal cases.
properties.plot_summary: A true-crime dramatization that follows the investigators who pieced together the case behind the brutal killings of the Richthofen couple. The film reconstructs police work, evidence gathering, and interviews that led to the prosecution of Suzane von Richthofen and the Cravinhos brothers.
